title: Tenant-affine KV microshard soft-sharing with bloom hints and DP scrubber
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a tenant-affine microshard layer on top of the existing GPU-resident KV cache to increase cross-request reuse while preserving tenant isolation and controlling memory fragmentation. The design uses small, fixed-size microshards (e.g., 8-32KB) that can be coalesced into GPU slab windows for continuous batching efficiency. A lightweight probabilistic bloom hint is exported per microshard so the router and prefetcher can detect likely matches without full fingerprint comparisons. To enable safe sharing across tenants where appropriate, we add a differential-privacy-based scrubber that masks sensitive tokens when a microshard is made eligible for soft-sharing. The feature aims to reduce cold KV fills and improve p50/p95 latency under mixed-tenant traffic while keeping worst-case p99 degradation bounded via per-tenant leases and eviction credits.
progress_updates: 2026-01-20: Spike complete — implemented microshard allocator prototype in runtime (local branch: feat/microshard-allocator). Verified basic allocation and coalescing into GPU slab windows.

2026-02-02: Router integration spike — router can consume bloom hints from SDK and route prefetch candidates. Simulated cross-tenant traffic shows 18% reduction in KV fills at steady state for synthetic conversational workload.

2026-02-18: Privacy review kickoff — design doc submitted to privacy channel for DP scrubber parameters (link in links). Initial recommendation: epsilon=1.0 per shard exposure window; scrub top-k most-sensitive token positions.

2026-03-03: Benchmark run against baseline runtime-1.18 on 4xA100, mixed small/large chat workload: p50 latency improved 9%, p95 improved 7%, p99 within 2% of baseline. GPU resident memory fragmentation decreased by ~11% after microshard compaction pass.
2026-03-10: Code PR opened for allocator and bloom hint serialization: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/3486 — CI failed on one flaky test related to slab-eviction race.
2026-03-10: Assigned Diego Fernández to debug eviction race and finalize API shape with SDK team.
decisions: Microshard size default: 16KB (configurable per model family). Chosen as tradeoff between metadata overhead and fragmentation risk.
Bloom hint: 512-bit keyed bloom filter (per-shard) serialized compactly to 64 bytes using sparse encoding in common cases.
Soft-sharing policy: default disabled per-tenant; opt-in via account setting. Account owners can enable 'soft-share' with DP scrubber applied before exposure to other tenants.
Eviction policy: hybrid reuse-score + lease-credit. Reuse-score increments on cross-request hits; lease-credit protects active tenant-owned shards for short windows during batch flush.
Storage format: store canonicalized KV payload compressed (LZ4) and quantized to FP16 by default; store separate INT8 delta for high-frequency small models to save memory on embed-heavy flows.
tradeoffs: Bloom hints reduce false full-fingerprint checks but add 64B per microshard. For very tiny shards and extreme multi-tenancy this can increase overhead; mitigated by sparse encoding and adaptive hint disabling.
DP scrubber prevents sensitive leakage but can reduce reuse in privacy-heavy customers; we expose knob to tune epsilon and scrubbed token positions, and default to conservative settings.
Lease-credit reduces p99 regressions but can slightly increase memory pressure; selected short windows (50-200ms) to balance.
Compaction during idle cycles reduces fragmentation but can contend with background GC/repairs on the CPU host. We schedule compaction work with low-priority QoS and backoff heuristics.
review_feedback: PM (Samir Patel): ask to add explicit telemetry events for shard-owner changes and cross-tenant hit reasons to help investigate customer impact.
Design (Kimberly Cho): requested a minimal UI surface for Console to show per-account soft-sharing status and observed reuse gains before enabling wide rollout.
Security (Lena Hoffman): requested formal threat model for shard metadata leakage via bloom hints; recommended keyed bloom with rotation and enforcement in network layer.
Eng (Ravi Malhotra): raised concern about allocator fragmentation when microshard sizes are heterogeneous — proposal to align microshards to power-of-two bins to simplify slab packing.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes microshard allocator behind feature flag and default-off soft-sharing control per account.
Router and prefetcher consume bloom hints and reduce full fingerprint checks by >=15% in synthetic mixed-tenant workload.
p95 latency improvements observed in lab for mixed chat traffic without p99 regression >5% over baseline.
Console shows per-account soft-sharing status and reuse metrics for at least the rollout cohort.
Security review completed and bloom-key rotation implemented.
tests_and_benchmarks: Synthetic 100k convo workload with 200 tenants: steady-state KV fill reduction 17% (95% CI ±1.8%).
Mixed small/long chat with 60% short-turns: p50 -9%, p95 -7% vs runtime-1.18 baseline on 4xA100.
Stress test: enabling soft-sharing across tenants with DP scrubber (epsilon=1.0) shows reuse drop of 12% compared to raw sharing, but privacy constraints satisfied per privacy audit checklist.
Memory compaction pass reduced fragmentation by 11% on average in mixed loads; compaction CPU overhead <3%.
CI regression: flaky test 'slab/evict_race_test' reproduces locally; creating follow-up bug ENG-882212.
